6. Detected anomalies

6a. Observed technical evidence

SPL-001 OBSERVED EVIDENCE LOW Isolated waveform discontinuity at 2.3000 s
Test C1 · LPC residual impulse vs. neighbourhood maximum · family waveform · 2.300 s (samples 101429-101429)

The prediction residual at sample 101429 is 6.4x larger than any residual value within 20 ms on either side; the waveform does not continue smoothly.

Observed measurements{'impulse_ratio': 6.393582, 'residual_value': 0.014636, 'sample_step': 0.014862, 'sample_step_dbfs': -36.558419}
Threshold / baseline{'ratio_threshold': 4.0, 'neighbourhood_ms': 20.0, 'guard_ms': 0.5}
Alternative explanations
  • Click, pop, plosive or percussive onset in the original sound
  • Digital dropout, buffer underrun or bit error in the recording chain
  • Clipping onset
  • A hard edit point (cut, insertion or gain step without crossfade)
Confidence limitations
  • Edits made at zero crossings with matching slope, or with crossfades, produce no impulse.
SIL-001 OBSERVED EVIDENCE MEDIUM Digital silence of 400 ms at 4.100-4.500 s
Test C5 · exact-zero sample run detection · family silence · 4.100-4.500 s (samples 180809-198449)

17640 consecutive samples are exactly zero in every channel, while the surrounding background noise is about -45 dBFS. A continuous acoustic recording would contain that background noise during pauses.

Observed measurements{'run_samples': 17640, 'run_ms': 400.0, 'surrounding_noise_floor_db': -44.592411}
Threshold / baseline{'minimum_run_ms': 10.0, 'noisy_context_threshold_db': -100.0}
Alternative explanations
  • Inserted silence (editing)
  • Noise gate or 'silence removal' processing
  • Recorder muting or pause function
  • Dropout in the recording chain
Confidence limitations
  • Dithered or noise-filled insertions are not exact zeros and are not detected by this test.
DUP-001 OBSERVED EVIDENCE HIGH Segment at 6.18-6.37 s duplicates 1.18-1.37 s
Test C6 · log-mel self-similarity + waveform NCC verification · family duplication · 6.184-6.370 s (samples 272724-280916)

0.19 s of waveform at 6.184 s matches the waveform at 1.184 s with a normalised cross-correlation of 1.00000. Independently produced sounds do not repeat sample by sample.

Observed measurements{'ncc': 1.0, 'source_start_s': 1.184218, 'copy_start_s': 6.184218, 'length_s': 0.18576}
Threshold / baseline{'ncc_threshold': 0.98, 'similarity_threshold': 0.92}
Alternative explanations
  • Copy-paste editing (copy-move)
  • Loop-based music production or sampled/repeated material
  • Synthetic or machine-generated signals with exact periodicity
  • Playback of the same recording twice within the scene
Confidence limitations
  • Copies that were re-filtered, time-stretched or mixed with other sound may fall below the NCC threshold.
ENF-001 OBSERVED EVIDENCE MEDIUM Mains-hum phase jumps by 2.13 rad near 2.32 s
Test C7 · frame-wise hum phase tracking (absolute time reference) · family enf · 2.170-2.470 s

The 50 Hz hum phase changes by 2.13 rad (122 deg) around 2.32 s, while it evolves smoothly elsewhere. Removing or inserting samples breaks hum phase continuity.

Observed measurements{'phase_step_rad': 2.132336, 'robust_z': 52.3432, 'hum_amplitude': 0.000133}
Threshold / baseline{'phase_step_threshold_rad': 0.35, 'z_threshold': 6.0}
Alternative explanations
  • Removal or insertion of samples (edit)
  • Change of the electrical environment (another power circuit)
  • Strong interference near the hum frequency
Confidence limitations
  • Edits that remove an exact multiple of the hum period leave no phase step.
  • Time resolution about +/- 0.2 s because of the narrow band-pass filter.

Test D4 · scope statement · family codec_metadata

Detecting how many times a signal was lossily encoded requires access to the codec's internal frame grid and quantiser (e.g. MDCT-coefficient statistics). SonicTrace measures the band-limit and spectral-hole fingerprints of *at least one* lossy generation; it does not count generations.

TopicStatusStatementSupportingAlternatives
lossy_codingnot_indicatedNo band-limit or spectral-hole fingerprint of lossy coding was measured.High-bitrate or dithered decodes can leave no measurable fingerprint

Independence rules: statistical findings never count as corroboration; level/spectral jumps and noise-floor changes are not counted again when digital silence explains them.

9. False-positive considerations

  • Digital silence is also produced by noise gates, 'silence removal' and recorder pause functions.
  • Level and spectral jumps occur naturally at speech and note onsets; they are reported only as supporting observations.
  • Clicks, plosives and percussive transients produce residual impulses similar to hard edits.
  • Loop-based music and synthetic signals repeat material legitimately.

10. Methodology limitations

  • Experimental: long windowed-sinc resamplers leave little periodic residual structure.
  • Thresholds were calibrated on synthetic data (calibration split) and have not been validated on casework.
  • Not-applicable tests provide no information either way.

11. Final evidence-based assessment

Observed technical evidence

  • SPL-001: Isolated waveform discontinuity at 2.3000 s
  • SIL-001: Digital silence of 400 ms at 4.100-4.500 s
  • DUP-001: Segment at 6.18-6.37 s duplicates 1.18-1.37 s
  • ENF-001: Mains-hum phase jumps by 2.13 rad near 2.32 s
  • ENF-002: Mains-hum phase jumps by 6.15 rad near 4.30 s
  • ENF-003: Mains-hum phase jumps by 0.76 rad near 6.02 s
  • ENF-004: Mains-hum phase jumps by 0.65 rad near 6.48 s

Statistical anomalies

42 statistical anomaly finding(s) (see 6b).

Possible explanations

  • EV-001 (2.32 s): Samples removed or inserted here: mains-hum phase continuity is broken at the same point as the waveform
  • EV-002 (4.30 s): Insertion of digital silence, or muting/gating, at this point
  • EV-002 (4.30 s): Samples removed or inserted here: mains-hum phase continuity is broken at the same point as the waveform
  • EV-003 (6.07 s): Copy-move edit: material repeated from elsewhere in the recording (or loop-based/repetitive source material)
  • EV-003 (6.07 s): Samples removed or inserted here: mains-hum phase continuity is broken at the same point as the waveform
  • EV-004 (6.46 s): Copy-move edit: material repeated from elsewhere in the recording (or loop-based/repetitive source material)
  • EV-004 (6.46 s): Samples removed or inserted here: mains-hum phase continuity is broken at the same point as the waveform

What cannot be concluded

  • Whether the recording is authentic, or whether it truthfully represents the events it appears to capture.
  • Whether any detected processing was performed with an intent to deceive; most processing (conversion, normalisation, noise gating, compression) is routine.
  • Whether the voice or content is synthetic/AI-generated: no test in this engine addresses speech synthesis.
  • That the file is unedited: the absence of indicators does not prove absence of editing. Crossfaded edits at matching levels, consistent backgrounds and re-recording can evade every test.
  • How many times the audio was lossily encoded (only the presence of at least one lossy generation is measurable).
  • Whether the audio was downsampled: downsampling leaves no trace distinguishable from a native recording at the lower rate.
  • Error rates on real casework: all performance figures come from a synthetic benchmark and are not real-world forensic accuracy.

Summary: Local edit indicators: STRONG. Structural/metadata inconsistencies: NONE. Processing history: no lossy-coding, upsampling or gain-change fingerprint indicated. These are indicator levels from explicit rules, not probabilities of manipulation.
